strongest_result: Accepted full-original-scope randomized polynomial-time congestion-1 AON approximation C log(k+2) exp(C sqrt(log log(k+4))) on every undirected unit-capacity graph with k indexed terminal pairs; always feasible output and at least 3/4 probability of the cardinality guarantee.
nearest_comparisons: CKS2005 Theorem 3.2 gives O(log^2 k) general-graph AON. The candidate improves the ratio to log^(1+o(1)) k without augmented congestion or restricted inputs.

BJS2026 Theorem 3.1 supplies the integral-node-weight decomposition and Conjecture 5.1 states the exact AON target. The candidate adds a fixed-path admission-preserving transfer; it does not add a new decomposition theorem.

CKS2005 Lemma 1.1 / Theorem 3.1 and corrected CKS2013 Section 3.4 supply uniformization and exact matching rounding. These substantial ingredients are prior work; the candidate contribution is their full-scope interface with BJS.
Anand2026 Theorem 5.1 / Appendix C improves decomposition overhead with different weight/parameter guarantees, but no equivalent AON resolution was located in its primary full text.

importance.reason: The theorem improves the full general-graph congestion-1 admission problem from the verified O(log^2 k) baseline to near-logarithmic approximation. Unit admission is a meaningful nonlinear objective and the improvement applies to the whole original input class.

novelty.reason: No equivalent original-scope algorithm was located in the bounded fresh primary search. The fixed-path cut charge combined with protected original bridges supplies the admission interface missing from a mere overhead substitution. All uniformization, decomposition and CKS rounding ingredients are explicitly prior work.

technical_depth.reason: The new proof is a compact composition of powerful established tools. Its interface is useful and mathematically substantive, but the record does not establish a new decomposition or rounding method, a matching lower bound, or technical depth comparable to strong broad STOC advances.

breadth_or_consequence.reason: The AON improvement itself is general and substantial, but no further algorithmic applications or broader transfer consequences beyond this single routing model are established in the frozen candidate. A concrete competitive breadth case remains unmade.

exposition_and_verifiability.reason: The main reduction and exact bit/success accounting are checkable, and independent finite diagnostics passed. The dossier mixes a precise known CKS theorem with an incomplete sketch of its corrected proof; the residual coverage convention and exact source pagination need clearer exposition. There is no completed manuscript or implemented BJS/CKS composition.

case_for_stoc: A full general-graph exact-congestion AON improvement of nearly one logarithmic exponent is a serious approximation-algorithms contribution. The attractive conceptual point is that one fixed prepared path family and protected admission cuts can bypass changing-throughput weights. That supports mathematical innovation acceptance. It does not yet justify all-strong venue judgments: most technical machinery is imported, and broader consequences and depth of the new interface are uncertain. The appropriate current internal assessment is working_paper, not submission_ready.
remaining_weaknesses: Technical depth of the new interface relative to the substantial known ingredients remains uncertain for competitive STOC evaluation.
No established consequence beyond the full AON improvement or broader structural transfer theorem is supplied.

Future exposition should cite CKS2005 Theorem 3.1 precisely, explain its corrected journal support and the residual-cluster coverage convention, and avoid treating journal Theorem 3.8 as an arbitrary-component black box.
The current equivalent-result search is bounded and source refreshes have disclosed access limits; no exhaustive priority finding is claimed.
Writing, clean build, citation, visual and release gates remain outside this mathematical referee job.
